text:
[RTIM.3.2.6] **A move does not visit the instants it skips.** Everything due
at or before the new instant is done at the new instant, and an expression that
reads the time reads the new instant. A harness that needs an effect to happen
at an earlier instant moves the clock to that instant and pumps there first,
which is how the `.dstest` interpreter walks a timeline ([RTIM.14.5]).

idris.name: rtim_3_2_6__alphas_five
idris.note: Five alphas, kinds 0 to 4. A fixture.

idris.name: rtim_3_2_6__one_move_timed
idris.note: ONE MOVE DOES EVERYTHING DUE: `Go`, a `Short` (TTL 2) and a `Long` (TTL 4) asserted at 0 and pumped arm the timer; one advance to 5 sweeps both TTL facts at the tick and the pump fires the follow-up, which mints `Fired` and takes the timer -- logical/RTIM.3.2.6_one_move_does_everything_due's shape. Executed: working memory holds `Go` and `Fired`. LESS than the clause: the sweep is at the tick and the timer at the pump, one pump boundary as the clause's 'done at the new instant'.

idris.name: rtim_3_2_6__rules
idris.note: `wait`, lowered: on `Go` with `after 3: emit Fired` -- the parent emitting the timer, the follow-up emitting `Fired` then retracting the timer. A fixture.

idris.name: rtim_3_2_6__tests
idris.note: The one-move program's tests. A fixture.

idris.name: rtim_3_2_6__ttl
idris.note: THE ONE-MOVE FIXTURE'S KINDS: `Go` an entity; `Short`, `Long` and `Fired` explicit with a TTL of 2, 4 and 100; the timer explicit with none. A fixture.
